ui.spellbookText: Everything you have learned so far:

filter.title: The Sorting Room
filter.blurb: Pick out exactly the marbles you want with filter.

boxes.title: Question Boxes
boxes.blurb: Ask many questions at once with and / or - and put a box inside a box.

numbers.title: Number Valley
numbers.blurb: Marbles with numbers! Compare them with > and <.

map.title: The Paint Shop
map.blurb: Change marbles with map: paint, grow and decorate them.

math.title: The Number Factory
math.blurb: Do math on the numbers inside the marbles.

reduce.title: The Counting Tower
reduce.blurb: Squash a whole stream of marbles into one number with reduce.

fold.title: Reduce Masters
fold.blurb: Build your own reduce, step by step.

extreme.title: The Volcano
extreme.blurb: Really hard puzzles: long chains of filters, maps and reduces, where the order of steps matters. Even grown-up programmers will sweat!

filter.title: filter
filter.text: A gate: keeps only the marbles that answer yes.

isnot.title: is not
isnot.text: Keeps every marble that is NOT red.

chain.title: many steps
chain.text: Marbles go through the steps from top to bottom.

and.title: and
and.text: An ALL box: every question in it must be yes.

or.title: or
or.text: A ONE-yes box: one yes is enough.

brackets.title: a box in a box
brackets.text: The inner box is answered first. In code, a box inside a box is written with ( brackets ).

negate.title: throw away
negate.text: Click "keep marbles where" to switch the gate around: it throws away the marbles that answer yes.

compare.text: > bigger than, < smaller than, >= bigger or equal, <= smaller or equal.

map.title: map
map.text: A machine that changes every marble.

mapif.title: map ... only if
mapif.text: Change only some marbles; the rest pass unchanged.

math.text: Math with numbers. "number" means the number the marble had before.

count.title: reduce count
count.text: How many marbles are there? Always the last step.

sum.title: reduce sum
sum.text: Adds up the numbers of all marbles.

maxmin.title: reduce max / min
maxmin.text: max finds the biggest value, min the smallest.

fold.title: reduce from
fold.text: Start total at 0. For every marble, total becomes total + number. The last total is the answer.

f1.intro:
Welcome to the Functional Marble Machine! You build a machine, and marbles roll through it.

Look at the examples on the left: **IN** is what goes into the machine, **OUT** is what should come out. Can you find the rule? Click an example to put it in the machine.

**filter** is a gate. It asks every marble a question. Marbles that answer *yes* roll on, the others drop out. This machine keeps blue marbles:

```
filter color is blue
```

Click the word **blue** in your machine, pick another color, and press **▶ Run this** to try it.
hints: You only need to change one word.
Which color is in every OUT?

f2.intro:
Now build the machine yourself! Press **+ filter** to add a gate, then click the words to change them.

Not sure what happens? Press **🐞 Step by step** and follow the marbles one by one. It's free!
hints: Add a filter step.
Which color survives?
Look at the colors in OUT.

f3.goal: Remove all yellow marbles. Keep everything else.
f3.intro:
Sometimes it is easier to say what you **don't** want. Click on **is** and choose **is not**:

```
filter color is not red
```

This keeps every marble that is not red.
hints: Which color never comes out?
Use "is not".
Which color is missing in OUT?

f4.intro:
Marbles come in three sizes: **small**, **medium** and **big**.

Click on **color** to ask about **size** instead:

```
filter size is small
```
hints: Colors don't matter here. Look at the sizes.

fb3.goal: Keep the marbles that are not big.
hints: Look at the sizes.
Which size never comes out?

f5.intro:
Some marbles have a pattern: **plain**, **striped** or **dotted**.

```
filter pattern is dotted
```
hints: Look at the patterns.

fb4.goal: Keep the marbles that have a pattern (not plain).
hints: Look at the patterns.
Which pattern never comes out?

f6.goal: Keep only the marbles that are red AND big.
f6.intro:
A machine can have many steps. Marbles go through them from top to bottom, like a conveyor belt with several gates.

```
filter color is blue
filter size is small
```

The first gate lets only blue marbles through. The second gate checks those blue marbles and keeps the small ones.
hints: Two things matter: color and size.
Use two filter steps.

f7.goal: Keep the small marbles that are not blue.
hints: Two gates again.
One gate for the size, one for the color.

fb5.goal: Keep the striped marbles that are not green.
hints: Two gates: one for the pattern, one for the color.

fx.goal: Keep the big marbles that are not red and are dotted.
hints: Three things matter: size, color and pattern.
One gate for each.

f8.goal: Keep the marbles that are green AND striped.
f8.intro:
One gate can ask several questions. Press **+ and** next to a question. Your questions go into a **blue ALL box**:

```
filter color is red and size is big
```

An ALL box says *yes* only when **every** question inside says *yes*. A big blue marble? "color is red" says no, so the whole box says no.
hints: Two things matter: color and pattern.
Press "+ and" next to the first question.

fc1.goal: Keep the marbles that are red AND small.
hints: Color and size, in one ALL box.

fa2.goal: Keep the marbles that are blue AND small AND dotted.
fa2.intro: An ALL box can hold as many questions as you like. Press **+ and** at the bottom of the box to add another one. Every single one must say *yes*.
hints: Three questions in one ALL box.

f9.goal: Keep the marbles that are red OR yellow.
f9.intro:
Press **+ or** to get an **orange ONE-YES box**. It says *yes* when **at least one** question inside says *yes*:

```
filter color is blue or color is green
```

Careful: two separate gates can't do this! The first gate would already throw away the marbles the second one wants.

Tip: click the title of a box to switch it between ALL and ONE-YES.
hints: Two colors come out.
Press "+ or" next to the first question.

fc2.goal: Keep the marbles that are big OR striped.
hints: A marble needs only one of two things to come out.

fo2.goal: Keep the red, yellow and purple marbles.
hints: One ONE-YES box with three questions.

fc3.goal: Keep the big marbles that are not blue.
hints: "is not" works inside a box too.

fg1.goal: Keep the red marbles that are big OR striped.
fg1.intro:
Now put a box inside a box! Build **color is red** and press **+ and**. Then, on the *second* question, press **+ or**:

```
filter color is blue and (size is small or pattern is dotted)
```

The machine answers the **inner** box first: "is it small or dotted?". Then the outer ALL box checks: "is it blue, AND did the inner box say yes?"

Use **🐞 Step by step** to see every box light up green ✓ or red ✗.
hints: The color must always be right. The other two things: one is enough.
A ONE-YES box goes inside the ALL box.

fc4.goal: Keep the dotted marbles that are red or blue.
hints: Two colors are fine, but the pattern must be right.
Start with the colors in a ONE-YES box... or start with the pattern.

fg2.goal: Team 1: big red marbles. Team 2: small blue marbles. Keep both teams!
fg2.intro:
This time the outer box is a ONE-YES box, with two ALL boxes inside - one for each team:

```
filter (color is green and size is small) or (color is yellow and size is big)
```
hints: Start with: color is red OR color is blue. Then press "+ and" next to each color to add its size.

fn1.goal: Throw away the marbles that are red AND big. Keep all the others.
fn1.intro:
A gate can also **throw away** marbles. Click on **keep marbles where** and choose **throw away marbles where**:

```
filter not (color is green and size is small)
```

This throws away the small green marbles. Everything else rolls on.
hints: Which marbles are missing in OUT?
Switch the gate to "throw away".

f10.goal: Keep the marbles that are big or dotted - but never purple ones.
hints: Big or dotted: a ONE-YES box.
The color is checked in an ALL box around it.

n1.goal: Keep the marbles with a number bigger than 5.
n1.intro:
These marbles have numbers on them! Click on **color** and choose **number**. Then you can compare: **>** means *bigger than*, **<** means *smaller than*.

```
filter number > 3
```

This keeps 4, 5, 6 ... but not 3 itself.
hints: Look at the numbers that come out. What is the smallest one?

n2.goal: Keep the marbles with numbers 3 or smaller.
n2.intro:
**<=** means "smaller or equal" and **>=** means "bigger or equal". This keeps 4, 5, 6 ...:

```
filter number >= 4
```
hints: What is the biggest number that comes out?

nb0.goal: Keep the marbles with numbers 7 or bigger.
hints: What is the smallest number that comes out?

n3.goal: Keep the marbles with even numbers.
n3.intro:
Even numbers are 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 ... and odd numbers are 1, 3, 5, 7 ...

```
filter number is odd
```
hints: Look at the numbers that come out. What do they have in common?

nb1.goal: Keep the odd numbers bigger than 4.
hints: Two things about the number.
Odd numbers, but not the small ones.

n4.goal: Keep the red marbles that have odd numbers.
hints: One question about color, one about the number.

n5.goal: Keep the marbles with numbers from 3 to 7.
hints: A number is "between" when it is big enough AND small enough.

nb2.goal: Keep the numbers smaller than 3 or bigger than 7.
hints: The middle numbers are thrown away.
A ONE-YES box with two questions.

n6.goal: Keep the marbles that are bigger than small.
n6.intro: Sizes can be compared too: small < medium < big.
hints: Two sizes come out. Try > with sizes!

nb3.goal: Keep the even marbles that are medium or big.
hints: One question about size, one about the number.

nx.goal: Keep the red marbles with even numbers - and every marble with a number bigger than 8.
hints: Big numbers always come out, whatever their color.
Two teams: (red and even) or (bigger than 8).

m1.intro:
**map** is a machine that changes *every* marble that goes through it. Press **+ map**:

```
map color -> green
```

Every marble's color becomes green. Nothing gets thrown away - map never removes marbles.

(Press **</> Code** to see your machine as code. In code, "becomes" is written as an arrow: ->)
hints: Compare the colors IN and OUT.
The colors stay the same. What changes?
Look at the patterns.

m3.goal: Make every marble purple AND dotted.
m3.intro:
One map can change several things. Press **+ change more**:

```
map color -> red, size -> small
```
hints: Two things change.
Use "+ change more".

m4.goal: Keep only the red marbles and paint them yellow.
m4.intro: Now combine the gate and the paint machine! First **filter**, then **map**.
hints: Some marbles disappear, and the ones left change color.
Two steps: filter first, then map.

m5.goal: Keep the small marbles and give them stripes.
hints: Some marbles disappear. Which ones?
filter first, then map.

m6.goal: Paint the big marbles red. Leave the others as they are.
m6.intro:
Press **+ only if...** to change only some marbles. The others pass through unchanged - nobody is thrown away!

```
map color -> green if pattern is dotted
```
hints: Not every marble changes. Which ones do?
Use "+ only if...".

mb2.goal: Plain marbles get dots. The others stay as they are.
hints: Only some marbles change. Which ones?

m8.goal: Every green marble becomes big. Then keep only the big marbles.
hints: First map (with only if), then filter.
Follow a small green marble with Step by step.

mb3.goal: Big or striped marbles are painted yellow.
hints: Only some marbles change.
"only if" can have a box with two questions.

m7.goal: Turn red marbles blue and blue marbles red.
hints: Careful - if you first paint red marbles blue, you can't tell them apart from the blue ones anymore...
Use a third color as a temporary parking spot: red → green, then blue → red, then green → blue.

x1.goal: Double the number on every marble.
x1.intro:
map can change numbers with math. Choose **number becomes**, then press **⊕ math**. Here **number** means "the number this marble had before":

```
map number -> number + 1
```

A marble with 4 becomes 5, a marble with 7 becomes 8.

Click on **+** to choose another sign: **+ − × ÷**.
hints: Compare each number IN with the one OUT: 2 → 4, 3 → 6...
How much bigger is each number?
Compare each number IN with the one OUT.

x3.goal: Every number becomes 10 minus the number.
hints: 1 becomes 9, 2 becomes 8, 3 becomes 7... What do the two numbers add up to?
Click on the first "number" and choose 10.

x4.goal: Every number becomes twice the number plus 1.
hints: There are two math steps: times something, then plus something.
Press ⊕ math twice.

xb2.goal: Every number becomes three times the number minus 1.
hints: Two math steps: times something, then minus something.

x5.goal: Every number is multiplied by itself.
hints: 3 becomes 9, 4 becomes 16...

x6.goal: Keep the even numbers and cut them in half.
hints: Some marbles disappear. Which ones?
filter first, then map with ÷.

x7.goal: Red marbles get 10 extra points. The others stay the same.
hints: Only some numbers change. Which marbles are they?

xb3.goal: Numbers smaller than 5 are doubled. The others stay the same.
hints: Only small numbers change.

x8.goal: Throw away the green marbles and multiply the others by 3.
hints: Some marbles disappear. Which ones?
Then look at the numbers.

xx.goal: Keep the odd numbers. Each becomes (number + 1) × 2.
hints: Some marbles disappear. Which ones?
Two math steps: first plus, then times.

r1.intro:
**reduce** squashes all the marbles into **one number**. Press **+ reduce**. The simplest one counts them:

```
reduce count
```

After reduce there are no more marbles - just a number. So reduce is always the last step.
hints: Count the marbles IN. Compare with OUT.
Only some marbles are counted.
filter first, then count.

rb1.goal: Count the marbles with a number bigger than 5.
hints: Only some marbles are counted.

r3.intro:
**reduce sum** adds up something for every marble:

```
reduce sum number
```
hints: Add up the numbers IN yourself.

r6.goal: Add up the numbers of the big marbles only.
hints: Only some numbers are added.
filter, then reduce sum.

r4.intro:
**reduce max** finds the biggest value, **reduce min** finds the smallest:

```
reduce min number
```
hints: Where can you find the OUT number among the marbles?
Where can you find the OUT number among the marbles?

r5.goal: Find the smallest number on a blue marble.
hints: Only some marbles take part.
filter first.
Add the numbers up yourself and compare with OUT.
The answer is always twice the sum.

r8.goal: Count the marbles that have a pattern (striped or dotted).
hints: Only some marbles are counted.
"Has a pattern" means it is not plain.
Only some numbers are added.

rx.goal: From the red or big marbles, find the biggest number multiplied by itself.
hints: Three steps: filter, map, reduce.
Which marbles take part? What happens to their numbers?

d1.goal: Add up all the numbers - using "reduce from".
d1.intro:
Time to see how reduce *really* works! You keep a **total**. It starts at some number, then every marble updates it:

```
reduce from 0 : total + number
```

Start with total = 0. For each marble: total becomes total + number. The last total is the answer.

Use **🐞 Step by step** to watch the total grow under each marble!
hints: Choose "from" in the reduce step.
Each marble should add 1 to the total.

db1.goal: Add up the doubled numbers - using "reduce from".
hints: Each marble adds twice its number.

d3.goal: You have 50 coins. Every marble costs as many coins as its number. How many coins are left?
hints: Start from 50, not 0!
Each marble takes some coins away.

hints: Start from 20, not 0.

dk5.goal: Add up the numbers of the big marbles - using "reduce from".
hints: Filter first, then add by hand.

dk6.goal: Count the marbles with even numbers - using "reduce from".
hints: Filter first, then count by hand.

dk7.goal: Triple every number, then add them up - using "reduce from".
hints: Map first, then reduce.

dk8.goal: Start at 2 and multiply by every number.
hints: Like multiplying them all, but starting from 2.

dk9.goal: Start at 1 and triple the total for every marble.
hints: 1 marble → 3, 2 marbles → 9 ...

dk10.goal: For every marble: total becomes total × 2 + number.
hints: Follow it with Step by step.

dk11.goal: Add up every number multiplied by itself.
hints: Each marble adds number × number.

dk12.goal: The answer is the number of the last marble.
hints: total doesn't have to be used in the new total!

dk13.goal: Start at 100. Every marble takes away twice its number.
hints: Start from 100. Then minus something.

dk14.goal: Multiply the numbers of the red marbles.
hints: Filter first. What do you start a product from?
Each marble adds its number, but 1 less.

dk16.goal: Add 1 to every number, then multiply them all.
hints: Map first, then reduce from 1.

z1.goal: Red marbles count double, blue ones count one more. What do they add up to?
hints: Change the numbers first, then add them up.
Use two machines with "if" - one for red, one for blue.

z2.goal: Add up the numbers, but no marble may count more than 5.
hints: Big numbers get squeezed down to 5 before adding.

z3.goal: Take the marbles above 3, take 3 away from each, and count the ones that are now even.
hints: Four steps: gate, machine, gate, count.
Watch out: the second gate sees the numbers after the machine changed them.

z4.goal: Swap the colors: red becomes blue and blue becomes red.
hints: If you paint red ones blue first, you cannot tell them apart from the old blue ones any more!
Use a spare color nobody uses (purple) as a hiding place for a moment.

z5.goal: Every number becomes its distance from 5.
hints: 9 is 4 away from 5, and so is 1.
Two machines with "if". The order matters - the second one must not touch what the first one changed.

z6.goal: Big marbles count triple, then green marbles count half (rounded down). What is the total?
hints: "/" throws away the remainder: 7 / 2 is 3.
A big green marble is first tripled, then halved.

z7.goal: Plain marbles are out. Striped ones double, dotted ones get one more. What is the biggest number?
hints: Gate, two machines with "if", then the biggest.

z8.goal: Red marbles get 10 more. Then every marble above 10 turns red. Add up the numbers of the red ones.
hints: Do it in exactly this order - the second machine sees the new numbers.
Four steps: machine, machine, gate, sum.

z9.goal: Spin the colors around: red becomes blue, blue becomes green, green becomes red.
hints: Like the swap, but with three colors - you still need one hiding place.
Hide one color in purple, move the other two, then bring the hidden one out.

z10.goal: Write the numbers next to each other: 3, 1, 4 makes 314.
hints: Each new marble pushes the total one place to the left.
Pushing one place left means multiplying by 10.

z11.goal: Write the numbers of the marbles that are not red next to each other.
hints: First a gate, then the "write next to each other" trick.

z12.goal: Read the marbles as a secret code: striped means 1, plain means 0. What number is it?
hints: It is like writing numbers next to each other - but with only 0 and 1, the place is worth 2, not 10.
Plain-striped-striped is 011, which is 3.

z13.goal: Count the marbles in a strange way: 1 marble gives 1, 2 give 3, 3 give 7, 4 give 15...
hints: Each marble doubles the total and adds one.

z14.goal: Each marble takes the total away from its own number. What is left at the end?
hints: The total does not grow - each marble replaces it.
With 2, 5, 3: first 2, then 5 - 2 = 3, then 3 - 3 = 0.

z15.goal: Every number becomes what is left after sharing it out in 4s.
hints: 14 marbles in bags of 4: 3 full bags, 2 left over.
"/" gives the full bags: 14 / 4 = 3. Bags times 4 is what fits; take that away from the number.

z16.goal: How many numbers can be shared out in 3s with nothing left over?
hints: There is no "divides by 3" question - build the remainder yourself, like in the bags puzzle.
Remainder 0 means it shares out evenly.

z17.goal: Add up the last digits of the numbers.
hints: The last digit is what is left after sharing out in 10s.

z18.goal: Every number becomes the sum of its two digits: 47 becomes 11.
hints: The first digit is the number / 10.
The second digit is what is left after sharing out in 10s. Add the two.

z19.goal: Sizes go around: small becomes medium, medium becomes big, big becomes small.
hints: A cycle needs a hiding place, but there is no spare size.
Mark the small marbles with a pattern, move the other sizes, then use the mark - and wipe it off at the end.

zx.goal: Swap red and blue, then the (new) red marbles count double. Keep the marbles above 6.
hints: Swap first, using purple as a hiding place.
Then double the red ones and use a gate.

lab.title: 🧪 Marble lab
lab.pitch: Build your own row of marbles and see what the machine should give back. Costs {stars} once - and then telling the rule costs only one more star.
lab.how: Click a marble to change it, + to add one. Below: what the rule makes of your row.
